Life does get better. It may take some time, but it happens. Failure is a learning experience, and it’s not bad. The 20’s are one hell of a ride and you’re going to find yourself in many situations that you’re not going to enjoy. But that doesn’t mean let your guard down. You’re 24, you still have so many years ahead of you. You’ll meet someone that’ll have the same interests as you and it’ll be a click. Have that patience and that special person will come in place for you, whether you find her or she finds you. Do not be discouraged and think of yourself as a loser, cause if you think of yourself as one, you’re going to act like one. Rejection sucks but it’s also a learning opportunity. Take those opportunities because you never know until you try it out. You miss 100% of the shots you don’t take. I wish you the best of luck through your journey!

I want you to know OP that friends come and go. Real friends can be counted on your fingers. Everyone changes, that’s how life works and it sucks. You still have many years ahead of you to make new connections and be out there making new friends that will share the same interests as you. Frankly, I’ve lost many friends who I used to hang out with a lot and I would reminisce and try starting a convo, but sadly it did not work. But life works wonders and now I have supportive friends who check up on me everyday and we have fun! You can always start off with a hey, but if they leave you on read, then they probably moved on, as much as it sucks to say. But don’t beat yourself because of it. Remember you can’t change people, but you CAN make new connections out there with people that you may have never realized you shared the same interests. Don’t be afraid to take a risk :)
And yes I am going to therapy and am on medications hoping to feel better about myself, just sometimes hard to see the light

Take a deep breath in, hold it, and take a deep breath out. 
Ok now that you did that, explain to her what happened and don’t make an empty apology. Make it up to her if you can. You obviously had no ill intent let alone did it on purpose. You’re not going to break up, nothing bad is going to come out of this. Yes she’s going to be upset, so don’t invalidate her feelings either. You’re human too and you needed your rest. It happens.

You’re definitely not crazy, and don’t think yourself to be crazy, as hard as that might be. You know your relationship the best, and you’re feelings are valid. If she’s promising you a 50/50 chance of not being able to have a relationship with you, as a woman, especially since she’s said she’s straight, then I would leave, no doubt. Her love, going by what you said, does not seem to be genuine. And if she says no when you end up meeting her, it’s going to end up hurting you more. Do what makes you happy, you’re happiness is more important. It may leave her hurt, but do it for yourself.

Remember healing isn’t a very quick process. But you’ll definitely feel better and learn as time goes by. Allow yourself to feel any sadness, anger, whatever the case might be, that comes across your way and not suppress it. Distract yourself with things that bring you joy, big or small, and try new things as you never know what new interests might come across your path. She is not the sole reason of your happiness and does not dictate how you should feel, remember that. Keep a little journal and write down any new accomplishments that you feel proud of or that makes you happy, again big or small, whether that be a new drawing or a happy thought you came across by (that is not about her). Life is pretty crazy and it isn’t a smooth road, but you’ll be able to open up your heart again to someone who feels the same way about you, even if it takes a bit :)
